title: Banyan Fleet prognostics onramp scratchbook
content:
Context and quick summary:
- Call 2026-02-27 w/ Banyan ops + platform (CTO: Elena Park, Lead SW: Arjun Rao). They run ~2k vehicles, telematics via custom gateways (CAN -> MQTT), intermittent LTE coverage, bursts when vehicles return to depot. Goal: predictive maintenance assistant + automated claims enrichment (OBD-II code normalization, fault triage, suggested parts).
- They want LLM-powered assistant to summarize sequences of telemetry events and recommend probable root causes; also to post-process technician notes into structured claims fields for their insurance partners.
- Constraints: sensitive PII in driver notes, strict retention rules (45 days raw telemetry), must run inside VPC for production, initial pilot can be on Dedicated or Private.

Call notes (raw):
- Typical event payloads: 40-120KB per burst (logs + recent telemetry slices). Need to trim to relevant windows.
- Connectivity: gateways buffer then forward; bursts up to 800 reqs/min during depot windows.
- Latency expectation: user-facing summary UI needs ~500ms p95 for single-vehicle query; background batch claims enrichment can be relaxed (<=30s).
- Throughput target: pilot supports 20 concurrent analyst sessions, spikes to 200 ingestion events/min for claim batches.
- Security: customer-managed KMS, SOC2/ISO required for production.
- Compliance: driver identity must be redacted before any hosted analytics.
- Model behavior: they favor conservative outputs (high precision), must have hallucination guardrails and citations to telemetry timestamps.

Initial technical requirements (rough):
- Private control plane + VPC peering; option to deploy Redwood Private at their AWS account (we discussed private deployment image).
- Dedicated GPU pool for low-latency interactive summaries. Autoscale for depot spikes.
- Preprocessor service to: (1) extract event windows, (2) run deterministic normalization (OBD-II -> canonical code set), (3) redact PII, (4) produce compressed prompt (token budget ~1500 tokens).
- Model: start with a high-quality open model family (e.g., mix of Llama-3-like variants) quantized to int8 for cost; keep a smaller cheap fallback for background enrichment. Need evidence of acceptable F1 on our prompt suite.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for recent vehicle context (last 24h) to reduce token re-send for repeated analyst queries. Consider per-vehicle cache key. TTL 24h.
- Batching: continuous batching for background claim enrichment; for interactive queries keep batching window <=10ms to maintain latency.
- Rollout: canary on 5% traffic to dedicated, monitor hallucination + latency + cost.

Gotchas / risks flagged during call:
- Payload size: untrimmed telemetry dumps blow token budget -> need robust truncation heuristics and highlight extraction (anomaly detector upstream).
- Depots cause extreme bursts; naive autoscale might take minutes -> need burst capacity (reserve warm pods) or use regional buffer + queuing.
- Intermittent connectivity means lookups for cached context sometimes stale; must show context timestamp in UI and prefer latest telemetry.
- PII redaction: free-text technician notes often contain driver names and phone numbers; regex-based redaction is insufficient. Discussed simple ML redactor step before submitting to Redwood hosted models.
- Auditability: insurance partners require traceable evidence for recommendation; must include telemetry snippets + model rationale. Need to store prompts & model outputs in audit store (encrypted) for 45 days.

Action items (who/when):
- Priya: draft pilot architecture diagram (Private vs Dedicated options) and estimate monthly cost ranges for both (due 2026-03-05).
- Miguel: prototype prompt compression heuristics (anomaly highlight -> 12–20 events) and a token-count bench for representative payloads (due 2026-03-04).
- Sara: security checklist for VPC deployment & KMS integration; confirm retention/archival requirements for audit store (due 2026-03-06).
- Arjun (Banyan): provide 3 anonymized sample telemetry bursts + 30 anonymized tech notes (safe-copy) by 2026-03-03.

Prototype design notes (brainstorm):
- Preprocessing pipeline: ingest -> anomaly scorer (lightweight model on edge) -> window selector -> OBD normalizer -> PII redactor -> compress into bullet timeline + key metrics (RPM spike, coolant temp, MIL codes).
- Prompt template idea: system: "You are a diagnostics assistant. Use only the provided telemetry snippet and codes to identify probable causes. Include supporting timestamps and a confidence score 0–1." user: [compressed bullet timeline] + "Return: 1) top 3 causes with timestamps, 2) suggested next checks, 3) spare part codes."
- Caching: per-vehicle embedding + metadata to accelerate similarity lookups for repeated issues. But embedding sensitive data -> must be encrypted and possibly stored in customer-owned DB.
- Fallbacks: define a cheap model (smaller quantized) for low-confidence results or for bulk background runs; set explicit fallback chain in routing policy so interactive queries prefer high-quality model and only fallback when latency SLO would be violated.

Monitoring & evals:
- Create prompt evals using the 30 tech notes + annotated ground truth from their senior techs. Track precision@1 for cause prediction, hallucination rate (assertions not present in telemetry), p95 latency, and cost per active session.
- Instrument token-level cost breakdown using Redwood Console; add regression alerts on hallucination and latency.

Open questions / decisions to clarify with Banyan:
- Exact retention window for prompts/audit (they said 45 days but insurance partner might ask for 90). Check contractual constraints.
- Are there any regulatory region constraints for data residency? Initial ops in us-east but Banyan has EU fleets.
- Will Banyan accept redaction in initial POC or require fully in-customer redaction before reaching us?
- SLA target: do they want 500ms p95 or is 1s acceptable? Need to agree.

Notes for internal follow-ups:
- Ticket: create ENG-2381 pilot epic (priority: high). Link PR for initial preprocessing: github PR attached above.
- Config knobs to prepare in Redwood: per-customer KV cache TTL, per-route model routing + fallbacks, burst capacity config with warm pods, audit-store retention toggle per-customer.
- Quick benchmark to run once Arjun shares samples: token counts for untrimmed vs compressed, latency on dedicated gpus (A100-equivalent), and quality checks vs our prompt suite.

Loose timeline (proposal):
- Week 0–2: receive samples, prototype preprocessing + prompt compression, run local evals.
- Week 3–5: deploy Private pilot in Banyan AWS account (small dedicated pool), onramp security review.
- Week 6–8: iterate, expand coverage, canary to 10% of production traffic.

Random scribbles / TODO:
- consider on-device anomaly scoring (edge) to cut payloads by ~60%
- ask infra: can we spin warm pod pool on Dedicated for predictable depot windows? (Tom B.)
- create small checklist for legal: sample data sharing agreement for 30 anonymized records.

End of scratchbook. Save as working doc; will tidy into a customer-facing one-pager after first prototype benchmarks.
